ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, place $\square ABCO$ in the Cartesian coordinate system $xOy$, where $O$ is the origin. If the coordinate of point $A$ is $(4,0)$ and the coordinate of point $C$ is $(1,3)$, then what are the coordinates of point $B$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Extend BC to intersect the y-axis at point D,\\
$\because$ the coordinates of point A are (4,0),\\
$\therefore$ OA = 4,\\
$\because$ quadrilateral ABCD is a parallelogram,\\
$\therefore$ BC $\parallel$ OA, BC = OA = 4,\\
$\because$ the coordinates of point C are (1,3),\\
$\therefore$ OD = 3, DC = 1,\\
$\therefore$ BD = DC + BC = 1 + 4 = 5,\\
$\therefore$ the coordinates of point B are \boxed{(5,3)},
